contested.Capacity: 18.6 (unchanged numeral — only the unit label is wrong)

validity.researcher_notes: Sheet records Capacity=18.60 with CapacityUnits='mtpa'. This is a gas TRANSMISSION PIPELINE, not an LNG plant, so mtpa (mass throughput, the LNG-plant unit) is the wrong unit family; the controlled vocabulary for a gas pipeline's design throughput is bcm/y (billion m3/year). energypolicy.ru (Wayback capture, verified) states explicitly: 'транссахалинский магистральный газопровод ... Протяженность трассы газопровода – 637 км, диаметр – 1220 мм, проектная мощность – 18,6 млрд м3/год' (design capacity 18.6 billion m3/year — i.e. bcm/y). The SAME article separately states the Sakhalin-2 LNG PLANT's output as '9,6 млн т/год' (9.6 million tonnes/year = 9.6 mtpa). en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sakhalin-II independently corroborates the LNG plant figure as '9.6 million tonnes ... per year'. So GEM's sheet appears to have taken the correct numeral (18.6, the pipeline's own bcm/y design capacity) but mislabeled its unit as mtpa — possibly by analogy/confusion with the LNG plant's separate 9.6 mtpa figure. The number 18.6 does NOT match the LNG plant's 9.6 mtpa under any obvious conversion, and does match the pipeline's own stated design throughput as bcm/y exactly. Filing as a spec/unit concern rather than silently changing CapacityUnits, per SOP (contested surfaces the exact backend column + proposed value for human review).
